nodes.summary: The model used to illustrate multi-head latent attention and its separate positional key.

nodes.name: DeepSeek‑V4‑Flash
nodes.summary: A model that combines a detailed recent window with compressed global history.

nodes.name: DeepSeek‑V4.1‑Flash
nodes.summary: A model whose global cache is shared across layers and whose local windows are layer-specific.

nodes.name: Fast Transformer Decoding
nodes.summary: The 2019 MQA paper linked in the dense-cache and shared-heads articles (arXiv 1911.02150).

nodes.name: DeepSeek‑V4‑Flash model card
nodes.summary: The model card linked in the article on compression and selection of older positions.

nodes.name: Earlier keys and values remain valid
nodes.summary: In causal decoding, appending a token leaves the information available to earlier positions unchanged. Their keys and values can be reused while the new query computes fresh scores.

nodes.name: A fixed cache can give different answers
nodes.summary: The query determines the attention weights assigned to the stored values. Changing only the query can therefore change their weighted sum.

nodes.name: Dense KV storage grows linearly with context length
nodes.summary: For one sequence with 32 layers, 32 KV heads, head dimension 128 and two-byte elements, the key and value tensors require 524,288 bytes per token.

nodes.name: Query heads can share stored KV banks
nodes.summary: Reducing the KV-head count reduces stored keys and values while retaining a separate attention computation for each query head.

nodes.name: Heads can score a shared latent directly
nodes.summary: Moving the content-key projection onto the query preserves the dot product and allows heads to score a shared stored latent. A separate positional key preserves rotary position information.

nodes.name: Compression and selection change different counts
nodes.summary: Compressing positions changes how many global entries are stored. Selecting a subset changes how many entries a query reads.

nodes.name: Four global writers average 2.5 entries per token
nodes.summary: In V4.1‑Flash, three encoder layers each write one global entry per pair of tokens, and one decoder layer writes one per token. Their rates sum to 2.5 entries per token over a long sequence.

nodes.name: Packed values and scale bytes sum to 356 bytes
nodes.summary: In the V4.1‑Flash global cache, the 512-channel main vector uses 256 packed-value bytes and 32 scale bytes. The 128-channel index key uses 64 packed-value bytes and four scale bytes.

nodes.name: Global KV grows by 890 bytes per token
nodes.summary: Multiplying the V4.1‑Flash average of 2.5 global entries per token by 356 bytes per entry gives 890 bytes per token. The total memory budget also includes the local window, weights and other overhead.

nodes.name: Head count can offset a longer prefix
nodes.summary: In the toy dense-cache budget, doubling context length while halving the KV-head count leaves the number of stored bytes unchanged when the other factors stay fixed.

The article works through the equality between projecting the latent and applying the transposed projection to the query.
CSA selects among finer summaries, while HCA can read all of its coarser summaries.
The article counts writers across layers that share their global cache and retain separate 128-token local windows.
The article prices the main vector at 288 bytes and the index key at 68 bytes, then sums them.
At one million tokens the global term is 890,000,000 bytes, equal to 890 decimal MB.
Moving from 4,096 tokens with eight KV heads to 8,192 with four leaves 512 MiB of cached KV tensors.
